title: Function-call JSON stability harness for post‑training INT8/FP8 quant & calibration replay
creator: Asha Rao
description: Build a focused stability and regression harness that validates function-call / JSON schema adherence after post-training quantization (INT8 and FP8) using calibration replay artifacts. The goal is to measure token-level divergence and schema drift across model variants and calibration checkpoints and automate detection of regressions that would break structured output consumers.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic harness can replay calibration inputs against float, INT8, and FP8 builds and produce comparable function-call JSON outputs.
We detect and classify schema violations (missing keys, type mismatches, extra fields) with a per-case severity and signal a failure when severity > P1 threshold.
Regression dashboard shows token-level divergence histograms and schema violation counts per model/quant-profile and per-calibration-run.
Automated nightly job uploads artifacts and posts a summary to #quant-validation with links to failing examples and suggested rollback candidates.
Create a small set (~250) of curated prompt+ground-truth function call pairs that cover edge cases (nested objects, optional fields, arrays, enum coercion) and run in CI for fast feedback.
notes: Focus on post-training quantization flows (no QAT) to match current runtime pipelines.
We will reuse existing KV/prefix caching traces to exercise streaming/function-call scenarios.
Severity buckets: informational (minor whitespace/type coercion), warn (enum mismatch or optional missing), fail (required key missing or malformed JSON).
Keep harness small and deterministic: seed RNGs, fix micro-batch sizes, and pin quant libs to specific wheel hashes for CI reproducibility.
steps: 1) Define the canonical function-call test corpus: merge curated prompts with production calibration replays (s3://redwood-calib-replays/eng/19834/v1.tar.gz).
2) Implement a lightweight runner that can invoke float, INT8, and FP8 artifacts behind the same API layer and capture token stream + final JSON output.
3) Implement schema diffing util: compare output JSON to expected JSON using strict type checks and path-level annotations (reporting path, expected type, actual type, token index).
4) Add token-level divergence metric using normalized edit distance and per-token logprobs to surface silent degradations.
5) Wire nightly CI job and Grafana dashboard; add Slack notifier to #quant-validation and a GitHub check on PRs touching quant pipelines.
6) Run a baseline sweep across rwd-7b-v2 float vs rwd-7b-int8 vs rwd-7b-fp8 with existing calibration checkpoints and capture baselines.
